model: FC series digital indicating controller (C/C5 option, Modbus ASCII)
applies_to: Shinko FCS-23A, FCR-13A, FCR-23A and FCD-13A with the C or C5 serial option; FCR-15A and FCD-15A have no Modbus (Shinko protocol only). Manual No.FC1CE11.
summary: The FC series are PID controllers with seven set value memories and a simple 7-step program mode. On the C (RS-232C) or C5 (RS-485) option they can speak Modbus ASCII, one 16-bit holding register per request. The map covers the seven memory blocks of SV, PID, alarm and output limits, step times, general settings, PV, MV and the status word.

addressing.note: Addresses are printed as hex (0000H) and go into the request unchanged; the manual's example frames read SV memory 1 at address 0000H and PV at 0099H.

source.title: Communication Instruction Manual FC series (C, C5)
source.pages: Modbus command table pp. 11-14; settings p. 3; specification p. 16

notes: Modbus ASCII only (no RTU). Function 03 reads exactly one register and function 06 writes one; multi-register reads are not supported.

All data are 16-bit two's complement. Values with a decimal point are sent as whole numbers without it; PV-type values (PV, SV, alarm values, SV and scaling limits) follow the decimal point place (0078H).
The Modbus addresses differ from the Shinko-protocol data items for the same setting (PV is 0080H in Shinko protocol but 0099H in Modbus).
Units of PID times, cycles and MV are not printed in the command table.
Items marked for certain models still accept writes on other models but do nothing.
The manual is inconsistent about address 0: the Modbus section says a unit set to 0 answers normally (no broadcast), while the general notes say broadcast commands get no reply.

integration.summary: Select Modbus ASCII as the protocol on the keypad and give each unit an instrument number; then read PV 0099H, OUT1 MV 009AH and status 009EH one register at a time with function 03, and write SV memory 1 at 0000H with function 06.
integration.enable: Requires the C (RS-232C) or C5 (RS-485) option on a Modbus-capable model. Set instrument number, communication speed and Communication protocol = Modbus ASCII on the keypad; none of these can be changed over the bus.
quirks: Modbus ASCII with 7 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit; RTU masters will not talk to it.
setup: Factory defaults: instrument number 0, 9600 bps, Shinko protocol.
Speeds 2400, 4800, 9600 or 19200 bps, selected on the keypad.
On RS-485 fit a terminator at the far end of the line.
gotchas: Send A3/A4 type before the alarm value: changing the type resets the value to 0.
AT Perform/Cancel returns an exception during PI or ON/OFF action, or if it repeats the current state.
EEPROM write life is about one million writes; avoid cyclic writes.
